problem: The comparison sign is missing, so the key condition reads as nonsense: "used with f n" (Section 2), "Accelerometer | f n" (table), "Why is an accelerometer used with f n?" (Q2). A student cannot tell whether f must be far below or far above fn, which is the whole point of the section.
fix: Section 2: "An accelerometer is a seismic transducer used with f ≪ fn, usually r below about 0.2." Table row: "Accelerometer | f ≪ fn | Acceleration | ...". Q2: "Why is an accelerometer used with f ≪ fn?"

problem: Damping near ζ = 0.6–0.7 is said to "flatten H near the low-frequency end". At r ≪ 1 the ratio H ≈ 1 whatever ζ is; the working band of an accelerometer is set by ζ at the upper end, where damping removes the peak near r = 1 and pushes the flat region to higher r.
fix: Write: "Damping near ζ = 0.7 removes the peak near r = 1 and extends the flat band to higher r, and it keeps the phase shift close to linear, so the waveform stays faithful. Too little damping gives a sharp peak at r = 1; too much damping slows the response." Make the same change in the Q6 answer.

problem: The symbol D appears in the trap ("H = 1/D", "Z/Y = r²/D") and in the Q4 answer, but D is never defined anywhere in the chapter.
fix: Define it once: D = √((1 − r²)² + (2ζr)²), the denominator of the response, then use H = 1/D and Z/Y = r²/D.
